claims.text: PbTe is a crystalline thermoelectric material.
Unmodified PbTe has a typical nanoscale precipitate distribution.
Tailored heat treatments or advanced deposition techniques can induce a well-defined spatial arrangement of coherent SRO precipitates in PbTe.
Lattice heat conduction dominates in PbTe from room temperature to intermediate temperatures under ambient or slightly elevated operating conditions.
The proposed processing produces a coherent SRO precipitate architecture within the PbTe matrix.
Engineered SRO precipitates act as phonon-scattering centers.
Scattering of phonons by engineered SRO precipitates reduces phonon scattering times.
Reduced phonon scattering times lower the lattice thermal conductivity.
PbTe containing engineered coherent SRO precipitates will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than standard PbTe containing no precipitates or randomly distributed or incoherent precipitates.
The proposed effect applies generally to crystalline thermoelectric materials in which lattice vibrations dominate thermal transport.
The effect may vary at very high temperatures.
The effect may vary when electronic heat conduction becomes significant.
Phonon scattering is sensitive to the specific spatial configuration of SRO precipitates.
